title: Microsoft 365 admin center: dedicated License Requests page for Microsoft 365 Copilot
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents the new page, its actions and the stated administrator roles, and the roadmap facts match. The older request-process path reaches the request list but could show the remaining steps to approval.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a dedicated Microsoft 365 admin center page for managing user-submitted Microsoft 365 Copilot licence requests.
claims.quote: We are introducing a new dedicated License Requests page in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center to help admins more easily discover, review, and manage Microsoft 365 Copilot license requests submitted by users.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; rendered table; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Billing > Licenses > Requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center reaches the existing self-service request process.
claims.quote: select Billing > Licenses. On the Licenses page, select the Requests tab. Select the row that contains the request you want to review. Assign licenses to each user through the default Approve the selected license requests option.
claims.fix: For the all-users approval route, extend controls[1].ui.path to 'Billing > Licenses > Requests > request > Approve the selected license requests > Approve'. Add to its note: 'Select all user checkboxes before choosing Approve.' Keep the existing qualification that this process is not confirmed as the new page. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/licenses/manage-license-requests.

claims.claim: Settings > Org settings > Services > Self-service trials and purchases > product > Do not allow blocks that product's self-service purchases and trials.
claims.quote: go to the Settings > Org settings page. On the Services tab ... select Self-service trials and purchases. ... select the product name. ... select Allow, Allow for trials only, or Do not allow.

claims.claim: The MSCommerce command Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <ProductID> -Value "Disabled" disables self-service purchases and trials for the specified product.
claims.quote: Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <ProductID> -Value "Disabled"

claims.claim: No API or automation for reviewing and approving or denying requests on the new page is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph license requests approve deny self service requests API beta admin center; Copilot license requests PowerShell Graph. Opened release notes, manage-license-requests and cloud-licensing-api-overview; no request-decision API found.

claims.claim: No API or automation for the existing self-service licence request process is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph license requests approve deny self service requests API beta admin center; Copilot license requests PowerShell Graph. Opened manage-license-requests and cloud-licensing-api-overview; assignment APIs do not document request approval or denial.

claims.claim: When a user attempts a self-service purchase of a blocked product, they can submit a licence request to an admin.
claims.quote: When a user tries to make a self-service purchase for a product that you blocked, they can submit a request for a license to you, the admin.

claims.claim: The November partner announcement says Copilot Chat limit notifications include an upgrade option in most organisations.
claims.quote: Upgrade options: In most organizations, the limit notification includes an option to upgrade.

claims.claim: Users can select that upgrade option to request a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence from an admin.
claims.quote: Users can select it to request a Microsoft 365 Copilot license from their admin, who can approve or deny requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The announcement ties the direct-purchase option in upgrade notifications to whether an organisation permits users to buy licences directly.
claims.quote: If the organization allows users to buy licenses directly, users might also see an option to purchase a license.

claims.claim: The announcement says admins can turn off direct purchases for each product.
claims.quote: Admins can turn off direct purchases for each product.
